name: The moat
text: A moat 190 metres wide runs right round the temple, 5.5 kilometres in all. It stands for the ocean round Mount Meru, home of the gods, and it kept the temple’s ground damp and firm.

name: The western gopura
text: The long gate in the outer wall, with three towers. Elephants could walk through the middle. Behind it a stone road runs 350 metres to the temple.

name: The libraries
text: Two small buildings on either side of the road, called libraries. Nobody knows what they held: scrolls, or sacred objects.

name: The Terrace of Honour
text: A cross-shaped terrace in front of the temple, where the king is thought to have met the people. Carved nagas, seven-headed snakes, guard the road.

name: The galleries
text: The outer gallery is 800 metres long and carved with scenes from Hindu epics and the king’s battles: the longest stone relief in the world. Two more galleries rise above it.

name: Angkor Wat
text: Built in the early 1100s for the Khmer king Suryavarman II, first as a Hindu temple and later a Buddhist one. Three levels rise to five towers, the middle one 65 metres high, in the shape of the mountain of the gods.
